newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee weakens on RBI dollar purchases.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee weakens on RBI dollar purchases.

text.p: The Indian rupee weakened to 35.765 per dollar in afternoon trade on sustained dollar buying by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) intervention, dealers said.
The rupee opened Friday steady at 35.705/710 to a dollar.
"There has been some pretty heavy buying," said a foreign bank dealer. "Earlier in the morning corporate demand pushed the rupee down to 35.72."
"But right now it's only RBI buying which is driving the market."
Dealers said the central bank bought forward dollars over a wide range.
"They (RBI) started with October-delivery and have bought up to next June," said a dealer.
The impact of RBI intervention pushed down the rupee further, dealers said. "RBI hit banks repeatedly, buying October and January dollars," a dealer said.
Dealers were speculating since morning about an RBI move to push down an overvalued rupee which had begun hurting exports.
"There is no evidence, but it (RBI's move) appears to be a pre-planned one," said a dealer at a European bank.
